script.title: How a German Horse Fooled Scientists Into Thinking It Knew Math
sentences: In 1904, a German horse became famous for solving complex math.
His owner, Wilhelm von Osten, claimed the horse answered by tapping his hoof.
Hans could calculate dates, work with fractions, and tell time.
A panel of thirteen experts investigated the animal and found no fraud.
But psychologist Oskar Pfungst ran a new set of tests.
When Hans could not see the questioner, his accuracy collapsed from eighty-nine percent to six percent.
The horse was actually watching subconscious facial tension, stopping his hoof when the human relaxed.
Hans never understood math; he was just an expert at reading human anxiety.
script.description: In 1904, a German horse named Clever Hans amazed experts by solving math problems. But a psychologist soon discovered his real secret.

claims_en: In 1904, a German horse named Clever Hans was publicly reported for answering arithmetic questions.
His owner Wilhelm von Osten claimed the horse gave answers by tapping his hoof.
Clever Hans could calculate dates, work with fractions, and tell time.
A 13-person commission investigated Clever Hans in 1904 and concluded no tricks were involved.
Psychologist Oskar Pfungst conducted controlled experiments on Clever Hans.
Clever Hans scored 89 percent correct when seeing the questioner but only 6 percent when unable to see them.
Pfungst showed the horse was reacting to subtle, involuntary tension and head movements of the questioner.
The Clever Hans effect demonstrated that the horse responded to human cues rather than understanding math.
